editorial.headline: Culture and Sport Administration Is Closed to Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: This government-administration activity spans cultural stewardship, recreation and sport—and is closed to PMA registration nationally and in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 84126 covers government administration in culture, the arts, recreation and sport. Its remit is broad but distinctly public: the guidance and development of museums, galleries, libraries, historic places and objects, cultural heritage, regional arts, recreation and sporting activity. It includes the work of government bodies responsible for youth and sport, as well as those responsible for culture and the arts. This is therefore an administrative government function, not simply the operation of a museum, gallery, library, cultural site, arts programme or sporting event.

The record does not list any business scale as open to this activity. That absence matters: there is no scale-based route set out here for registration. The defining point is the nature of the work itself—government administration and public stewardship across cultural, recreational and sporting fields. Anyone assessing the code should read its scope as an institutional mandate covering the development and administration of those areas, including heritage and regional artistic activity.

Nationally, the PMA position is closed. The foreign-ownership ceiling is 0%, under the stated Presidential Regulation sources. In practical terms, foreign investment has no ownership space within this activity’s national PMA treatment. This is not a code whose public-facing cultural or sporting subject matter changes its investment classification: the record’s national position remains unequivocally closed.

Bali reaches the same result. A foreigner cannot register this activity through PMA in Bali today: the Bali status is closed and the record marks it as blocked. The Bali-wide rule permanently blocks PMA for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities, but this activity’s stated reason places it at medium-high or high risk and says it is not blocked by that moratorium. Its Bali restriction therefore should not be attributed to the moratorium. The record also calls for verification by address, an important practical check when applying the Bali position to a specific location.
